summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted for a recurrent flare characterized by severe epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Her symptoms began three days prior, with pain more intense than previous episodes. Lab results showed a mildly elevated lipase of 94 and normal liver function tests. Abdominal ultrasound was normal, with no gallstones or fluid collection. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and low-dose IV hydromorphone for pain. Nausea was controlled with PRN antiemetics. She gradually advanced to a soft diet, tolerated oral medications, and showed steady improvement. Her mental health medications were continued throughout. She was discharged home on day three with instructions to follow up with her GI and primary care providers, a short course of oral hydromorphone for breakthrough pain, and continuation of home medications for reflux, constipation, and psychiatric conditions.
